contradicting_evidence: Settled BTC and ETH ETF outflows improved substantially versus the prior packet, reducing one source of selling pressure without reversing it.
The latest completed-hour prices exceed earlier spot snapshots, showing that rebound demand can emerge even while the latest hour declines.
Many constituents outperform BTC or ETH, and settled BTC dominance is lower versus the prior packet; these observations argue against assuming uniform relative altcoin deterioration.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A choppy downward bias is favored while liquidity contraction and weak participation persist. Rebounds may stabilize prices temporarily, but broad recovery requires evidence beyond reduced outflows and relative outperformance during losses. ETH and the broader alt market lack confirmed transmission support.
falsification_conditions: A sustained sequence of higher prices is accompanied by broader absolute advances and improving ETH/BTC.
Subsequent eligible ETF observations turn supportive while stablecoin contraction eases, with price and spot-flow confirmation.
Independent breadth evidence confirms durable expansion rather than merely less-negative relative performance.
missing_evidence: Repeated price, spot-flow and breadth observations across the forecast window.
Further eligible settled ETF sessions and updated liquidity observations; current flows cannot be assumed to persist unchanged.
A recent macro trend rather than isolated levels, and source-qualified forward catalyst details.
supporting_evidence: The latest final ETF session remains negative: BTC -$124.5 million and ETH -$13.2 million.
Stablecoin supply contracted approximately 0.30% over 1d, 1.55% over 7d and 6.29% over 30d; deployment confirmation is not established.
Breadth is weak in absolute terms. Large-, mid- and small-alt proxy median returns are all negative, so relative resilience does not establish positive capitalization transmission.
ETH underperformed BTC in both the supplied 24h returns and the latest completed hour, weakening the case for broad risk expansion.
The supplied VIX and Treasury-yield levels describe a demanding risk backdrop, although their dated observations do not establish a fresh macro shock.
